report.source_text: Histopathology of the mitral valve demonstrated fibrosis, extensive acute and chronic inflammation, and necrosis. Gram’s stain showed numerous Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains. The aortic valve lesion that was initially interpreted as a Lambl’s excrescence also demonstrated necrosis, inflammation, and Gram-positive cocci.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old man presented with a three-month subacute course of constitutional symptoms (dyspnea, fatigue, weight loss), immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis (low C3, AKI, active urinary sediment), and systemic embolization (petechial rash). Initial evaluation suggested autoimmune vasculitis, leading to methylprednisolone therapy with partial response. Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated mitral valve vegetations (E006), prompting discontinuation of immunosuppression and initiation of intravenous ceftriaxone after blood culture positivity (E008). The patient underwent bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement and aortic valve debridement on hospital day 14 (E011). Histopathology of excised valve tissue demonstrated fibrosis, acute and chronic inflammation, necrosis, and Gram-positive cocci in pairs and short chains (E011). Following surgical intervention and antibiotic therapy, the patient demonstrated clinical recovery with renal function normalization (creatinine 1.2 mg/dL) and was discharged on hospital day 25 to complete four weeks of intravenous penicillin (E012).
